harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created the dedicated inventorysvc system account, installed /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service running /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker as that unprivileged user, enabled and started it, then verified persistence across a full node1 reboot (boot_id changed, service auto-started under inventorysvc post-boot).
actions_performed: Inspected /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker and confirmed no pre-existing inventorysvc account
Created system user 'inventorysvc' (no home, nologin shell) via sudo useradd --system
Wrote /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service with User=inventorysvc Group=inventorysvc ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker
systemctl daemon-reload, enable --now inventory-worker.service
Verified running process (PID 2922) owned by inventorysvc/inventorysvc, not root
Captured pre-restart boot_id and service enabled/active baseline
Issued backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' on node1 so the ack returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again
Confirmed boot_id changed (e4e401d2... -> fb6d915e...), proving an actual reboot occurred
Verified inventory-worker.service is enabled and active post-reboot, running as inventorysvc/inventorysvc (new PID 836)

evidence.requirement: os-comparison-worker running as managed service inventory-worker under dedicated inventorysvc account
evidence.summary: Confirmed binary present, created system account inventorysvc, installed and enabled the systemd unit, and verified via ps that the running process (PID 2922/2923) is owned by user/group inventorysvc, not root.
Captured boot_id e4e401d2-3dd8-48c6-848a-545631b9e229 plus systemctl is-enabled/is-active=enabled/active for inventory-worker.service before reboot.
Issued backgrounded 'shutdown -r now'; command returned and the SSH session was subsequently closed by the remote host, confirming the reboot was underway.

evidence.requirement: node1 changed boot identity proving actual restart
evidence.summary: Polled node1: first attempt got connection refused (node down), second attempt returned boot_id fb6d915e-fc05-4a97-84b8-366f826c0ba6, different from the pre-restart boot_id, proving the kernel actually restarted.
After reboot, inventory-worker.service is enabled and active (new PID 836), with the worker and its sleep child both running under user/group inventorysvc, confirming automatic recovery on boot.
